page: Amazon Web Services m6a.32xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The instance is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7R13 processor clocked at up to 3.6 GHz, providing 128 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 64 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU subsystem features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, with hardware support for AES, VAES, SHA-NI, and AVX instructions, though AVX-512 extensions are absent. It is paired with 512.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated GPUs or local NVMe storage, relying entirely on network-attached storage while offering a 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-core throughput and memory performance. In multi-threaded compute evaluations, the m6a.32xlarge achieves a top-tier stress-ng score of 191,273.61 and a PassMark CPU score of 99,308.37, driven by strong extended instruction execution (117,704.72) and cryptographic performance (151,639.74). Single-core metrics are moderately rated, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2,974.78 and a Geekbench single-core result of 1,734.0. Memory subsystems provide strong bandwidth, delivering 9,076.97 GB/sec in cached small-block reads and 252.01 GB/sec in uncached large-block reads, alongside strong database operations scores and an outstanding 129.17 million operations per second in Redis SET testing.

From an efficiency perspective, the m6a.32xlarge offers high thread density and extensive compute parallelism for scaled-up enterprise workloads without requiring specialized accelerator silicon. The primary technical tradeoffs stem from the absence of bundled local NVMe disks, which necessitates external storage planning, and average single-thread performance compared to higher-frequency compute-focused offerings. The platform is best fitted for high-concurrency microservices, in-memory caching platforms like Redis, enterprise database backends, Clang compilation pipelines, and multi-threaded ETL data processing tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services m6a.32xlarge is a high-capacity general-purpose instance featuring 128 dedicated vCPUs from a 64-core AMD EPYC 7R13 processor running at 3.6 GHz on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. Configured with 512.0 GB of DDR4-3000 memory, the platform maintains a standard 4:1 memory-to-core ratio alongside 50 Gbps baseline networking. The instance omits local NVMe storage and dedicated GPUs. Benchmarks demonstrate top-tier multi-threaded compute and encryption performance, evidenced by a PassMark CPU score of 99,308.37, a Geekbench multi-core score of 15,873.0, and high-performance in-memory caching reaching 129.17 million Redis SET operations per second. While single-threaded speeds and data compression hover around platform averages, the sheer core count and memory bandwidth deliver dense computational scaling suitable for enterprise application tiers, distributed databases, large-scale CI/CD software builds, and high-throughput network workloads.
